example_user_query: I've had a mild sore throat and runny nose for 2 days, what should I do?
summary_in_own_words: the patient has cold and sore throat and maybe a little feverish can be healed at home by taking medicine
red_flag_notes: Escalate to GP if: not improved after 1 week; very high temperature/feeling shivery; weakened immune system; sore throat with rash/bruising; difficulty breathing/swallowing/drooling

example_user_query: I got a small cut on my hand while cooking, how do I look after it at home?
summary_in_own_words: Stop any bleeding by applying pressure with a clean cloth or bandage, then clean the wound under running tap water (avoid antiseptic, as it can damage tissue and slow healing) and cover with a plaster or dressing
red_flag_notes: Escalate if: bleeding won't stop with pressure; signs of infection; something embedded that can't be safely removed

example_user_query: My eyes are itchy and I keep sneezing, is this just hay fever?
summary_in_own_words: The patient is likely allergic to pollen has blocked nose and headahe
red_flag_notes: Escalate to GP if: over-the-counter treatments aren't controlling symptoms; check if this could instead be worsening asthma

example_user_query: I think I might have a UTI, burning when I pee, what should I do?
summary_in_own_words: The patient feels burning sensation while peeing and has blood in the pee sometimes and feel tired
red_flag_notes: Escalate (111/GP) if: symptoms of a kidney infection (fever, back/side pain, confusion) -- this can indicate sepsis risk

example_user_query: I have a small red rash from an insect bite, it's not spreading, what should I do?
summary_in_own_words: The skin will be red and swollen might need to use the insect bite cream
red_flag_notes: CALL 999 if: difficulty breathing, swelling of lips/tongue/throat/face, feeling faint, collapse, confusion -- signs of anaphylaxis

example_user_query: I keep getting heartburn after meals, is this something I can treat myself?
summary_in_own_words: The patient feels painful burning in the chest, feel bloated and sick and constant burping and farting
red_flag_notes: Escalate to GP if: recurring indigestion plus food getting stuck when swallowing, unintentional weight loss, or persistent vomiting -- possible sign of something more serious

example_user_query: I've had a cough for over 3 weeks now, should I be worried?
summary_in_own_words: A cough usually clears up on its own within 3 to 4 weeks; in the meantime, rest, drink plenty of fluids, and try hot lemon with honey or ask a pharmacist about cough treatments -- see a GP if it lasts longer than 3 weeks
red_flag_notes: See GP if: cough over 3 weeks, very bad/worsening cough, chest pain, losing weight, swollen neck glands, hard to breathe, weakened immune system. See GP URGENTLY if coughing up blood

example_user_query: My lower back has been hurting for about a week, no injury, what should I do?
summary_in_own_words: The back pain can also be caused by a muscle pull or slip disc or it can be a serious long term problem
red_flag_notes: Get urgent help (111/A&E) if: numbness around genitals/buttocks, loss of bladder/bowel control, leg weakness, chest-area pain -- possible cauda equina, a rare but serious emergency

example_user_query: I've been really tired and lost some weight without trying, for a few weeks now
summary_in_own_words: It can be due to mental health conditions,digestion problem,hormone condition or poor nutrition
red_flag_notes: See GP as soon as possible, especially if weight loss is ongoing and unexplained -- important to identify cause early

example_user_query: My 3 year old has a high fever and won't settle, what should I do?
summary_in_own_words: A high temperature is 38C or above and is very common in young children -- most fevers can be looked after at home and settle within a few days; call 111 if the parent remains worried, the child seems seriously unwell, or other red-flag signs are present
red_flag_notes: Verify exact red/amber criteria on the real page -- generally: under 3 months old with any fever, non-fading rash, or child seems seriously unwell needs urgent same-day help

example_user_query: I bumped my head, I'm a bit dazed but talking normally, do I need to go to hospital?
summary_in_own_words: Head injury can cause concussion , vomitting so these are the symptoms
red_flag_notes: CALL 999 / A&E if: loss of consciousness, vomiting, seizure, clear fluid from ears/nose, worsening headache, behaviour change -- call 111 for advice under 5 years old

example_user_query: My asthma has suddenly gotten worse today, not sure how urgent this is
summary_in_own_words: The patient has shortness of breath and it can be triggered by exercising,cold or allergic reaction
red_flag_notes: CALL 999 if: reliever inhaler isn't helping, or severe difficulty breathing/talking -- an asthma attack can be life-threatening

example_user_query: I think I might have broken my wrist, it's swollen and I can't move it properly
summary_in_own_words: The patient has a broken arm and it needs fracture needs immmediate attention
red_flag_notes: Get medical help as soon as possible -- if severe (bone visibly deformed, through skin) call 999 instead of self-transporting

example_user_query: I have a deep cut on my leg and it won't stop bleeding even with pressure
red_flag_notes: CALL 999 if: bleeding doesn't stop with firm direct pressure after several minutes, spurting/arterial bleeding, or object embedded in wound

example_user_query: I'm having a bad allergic reaction, my face is swelling up but I can breathe fine
summary_in_own_words: Facial or lip swelling without any breathing difficulty needs urgent care but is not yet anaphylaxis; if breathing becomes difficult, the throat/tongue swells, or the person feels faint at any point, this becomes anaphylaxis and needs 999 immediately
red_flag_notes: CALL 999 IMMEDIATELY if breathing becomes difficult at any point, or symptoms progress -- this is the line between A&E and anaphylaxis/999

example_user_query: I have sudden severe chest pain and I'm having trouble breathing
summary_in_own_words: The symptoms are chest pain , short of breath , feeling sick , sweating and pale skin
red_flag_notes: Call 999 immediately -- do not wait to see if it passes; chew aspirin only if available and not allergic

example_user_query: My dad's face suddenly looks droopy on one side and his speech is slurred
summary_in_own_words: Use the FAST test: Face drooping on one side, Arm weakness, Speech slurred or difficult to understand -- Time to call 999 if any one of these appears, even if it later improves. Other possible signs include sudden vision loss, confusion, or severe headache
red_flag_notes: Call 999 immediately on ANY single FAST sign (Face/Arms/Speech) -- even if symptoms pass, still call 999, this could be a TIA warning sign

example_user_query: Someone has collapsed and isn't breathing normally
summary_in_own_words: Call 999 immediately and start CPR straight away, even if untrained -- if not confident giving rescue breaths, do hands-only chest compressions instead; the 999 call handler will talk you through it
red_flag_notes: Call 999 immediately and start CPR -- do not mistake occasional gasping (agonal breathing) for normal breathing
